draft.title: Policies and procedures
card: a rule or guide for decisions, such as a bullying policy. It says what the business expects and what is not allowed.
the steps to follow to carry out a policy or a task. It says who does what, and in what order.
A bullying policy might state that bullying is not tolerated. Its procedure might set the steps for making a complaint, such as who to report to and how the report is handled.
Both help a business obey the law and set routines, so staff handle the same situation in the same way.
draft.remember: A policy guides decisions. A procedure sets the steps to follow.

a.q: Which of these is a procedure rather than a policy?
opts: Steps for staff to report a workplace injury to a manager
A statement that the business will keep a safe workplace
A rule that discrimination is not allowed in the business
A guide that staff should treat all customers with respect
a.why: A procedure sets out steps, here the steps for reporting an injury. The other three state what the business expects or allows, so they are policies that guide behaviour and decisions.
a.clue: Which one lists steps to follow?

b.q: Dev runs a bakery in Geelong. He wants staff to handle food the same safe way every day, and to help the bakery obey food safety law. Which choice does this best?
opts: Write a food safety policy and a procedure with set steps
Write a food safety policy and let each worker pick the steps
Write steps for cleaning only, with no stated expectations
Tell staff in person each morning what the day's rules are
b.why: A policy states the expectation, and a procedure sets the steps, so together they give the same routine every day. A policy alone leaves each worker to choose the steps, so routines may differ.
b.clue: Which choice gives both the rule and the steps?

proposal.title: Policies and procedures
card: a rule or guide for decisions, such as a bullying policy. It says what the business expects and what is not allowed.
the steps to follow to carry out a policy or a task. It says who does what, and in what order.
A bullying policy might state that bullying is not tolerated. Its procedure might set the steps for making a complaint, such as who to report to and how the report is handled.
Both help a business obey the law and set routines, so staff handle the same situation in the same way.
proposal.remember: A policy guides decisions. A procedure sets the steps to follow.

a.q: Which of these is a procedure rather than a policy?
opts: Tell a manager, then fill in an injury form by end of shift
The business will keep its workplace safe for all staff
Discrimination of any kind is not allowed in the business
Staff are expected to treat every customer with respect
a.why: This option tells staff who to go to and what to do in order, which is what a procedure does. The safe workplace statement is tempting because it is about injuries too, but it only states an expectation, so it is a policy.
a.clue: A policy says what is expected. What does a procedure add?

b.q: Dev runs a bakery in Geelong. He wants staff to handle food the same safe way every day, and to help the bakery obey food safety law. Which choice does this best?
opts: Write a food safety policy and a procedure to carry it out
Write a food safety policy and let each worker choose how
Write cleaning steps only, with no stated food safety aims
Tell staff in person each morning what the day's rules are
b.why: A policy states what the bakery expects, and a procedure sets the steps, so staff follow the same routine every day. A policy alone is tempting, but if each worker chooses how to meet it, routines may differ from person to person.
b.clue: Think about what makes every worker act the same way.
